title: SSE continuation codec + delta framing for resumable streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a continuation-aware SSE framing codec and delta-chunk format to make streaming responses resumable, bandwidth-efficient, and safe for structured outputs (function/tool call payloads). This ticket implements server-side framing, resume tokens, and a thin compatibility shim so older clients (chunk-per-event assumptions) can continue to operate without changes.
background: We currently stream model output as a sequence of generic SSE events where large structured payloads (JSON for function calls or structured outputs) may be split arbitrarily across events. Clients that disconnect must either start over or rely on heuristic reassembly. This leads to user-visible regressions for long function-call bodies and brittle client parsers. Prior tickets improved reconnection behavior but did not add a compact delta format or an explicit continuation protocol for structured boundaries.
proposed_solution: Introduce a small framing layer on top of SSE with explicit event types and sequence semantics: METADATA, DELTA, CHECKSUM, RESUME. Each stream will open with a METADATA event containing stable stream_id and content_schema. Subsequent payloads are emitted as DELTA frames containing a monotonic sequence number, byte-range offsets (relative to the logical payload), and either a full chunk or a delta patch. Periodically emit CHECKSUM frames (rolling 64-bit XXHash) covering the last N bytes to allow efficient validation on resume. When a client disconnects, the server advertises a single opaque RESUME token: base64("stream_id|last_sequence|checksum") signed with a server key. On reconnect the client supplies resume_token and optionally a next_expected_seq; the server replies with a short resume handshake and continues with the next DELTA frames. To preserve compatibility, also support an outbound "compat/legacy" mode where the server coalesces DELTA frames into per-event SSE payloads that match the older chunk-per-event shape. The compatibility shim is opt-in by per-connection negotiation (Accept header or query param).
technical_notes:
- Frame types (literal strings): METADATA, DELTA, CHECKSUM, RESUME, END.
- DELTA payload envelope: sequence:int | offset:int | is_patch:bool | payload:bytes (payload base64 in HTTP event).
- Sequence numbers monotonic and 64-bit to avoid wrap in long-lived streams.
- Checksum window defaults to 8KB and frequency is configurable by profile.
- Resume token format: base64url(HMAC_SHA256(server_k, stream_id + '|' + last_sequence + '|' + window_checksum)). Token expires after 5 minutes by default.
- Function-call / structured outputs: we guarantee that logical structured payloads are annotated with content_schema in METADATA and will not emit boundary-splitting markers inside a JSON token. Instead we emit DELTA with offsets referencing the logical payload; this makes it possible for clients to reassemble without ambiguity.
- Backpressure: the server will continue to use continuous batching but must preserve sequence ordering per stream.
- Metric additions: streaming.resume.attempts, streaming.resume.success, streaming.resume.latency_ms, streaming.delta.bytes_saved.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-1.22.canary. 2) Enable for internal canary tenants (redwood-internal) for 48h. 3) Observe resume success rates and average resume latencies. 4) Enable compat/legacy mode by default for existing customers; require opt-in to strict continuation mode for new customers initially. 5) Full ramp to default continuation semantics after 4 weeks or when resume success > 99.5% and no customer regressions found.
testing_plan: Unit tests for encoder/decoder: sequence handling, checksum windows, resume token validation. Integration tests: simulate mid-stream disconnects under varying network loss patterns, validate that resume token replays resume from expected offset, and ensure function_call JSON reassembly matches original complete payload. E2E: instrument a client (node + python) to validate legacy compat mode and strict continuation mode and run against canary and staging. Load test to ensure no throughput regression: target <=3% p99 latency change under same QPS.
acceptance_criteria:
- Server emits METADATA at stream start with stable stream_id.
- Resume token is generated on client disconnect and can be used to resume within 5 minutes.
- Reconnect with resume_token returns the remaining bytes starting at last acknowledged offset (within one DELTA window).
- Function-call structured payloads are reassembled by clients without JSON parse errors after resume.
- Legacy compat mode reproduces prior chunk-per-event shape for clients that request it.
- Metrics show <1% failed resumes for canary tenants after 48h.
- Security review completed and token format documented in confluence.
- PR merged and runtime-1.22.canary image published with feature flag.
